S1.notes: Agent fails to correctly parse or cross-reference structured tool results. Common retail pattern: agent selects a wrong item variant after checking the product catalog (A31: picked flight that did not match user criteria; R1: wrong refund amount after exchange because it mistracked which items came from which order; R5/R6: wrong variant in exchange despite catalog lookup; R20: upgraded wrong item in order). In airline: agent miscalculates upgrade prices or misidentifies which reservation/flight leg is affected (A10: wrong upgrade amount; A14: misidentified cheapest business option for multi-leg reservation).

S2.notes: Agent calls the right tool but with wrong argument values. A8: booked two passengers but did not pass correct seat preference args. A12: passed wrong bag count in modify_reservation call. A17: attempted to charge gift_card even though previous tool call showed insufficient balance. R21: passed user-stated item ID 4107812777 directly to exchange tool instead of resolving the actual item ID in the order (9791469541), which caused a tool error. R76: repeated malformed tool calls leading to too_many_errors termination.

S3.notes: The most common failure mode across both domains. Agent completes some sub-tasks but drops others, or sequences them incorrectly. Retail: agent processes first item/order exchange successfully but then fails on second (often because first action changed the order status to 'exchange requested', blocking subsequent actions on the same order). Airline: agent completes flight rescheduling but drops the baggage add, or completes one reservation cancellation but not others. Also includes cases where agent stops after one action when multiple were clearly requested (A16: only updated flight, missed certificate add; A35: cancelled flight but booked new one with wrong passenger count).

S4.notes: Two sub-patterns: (1) Agent executes an action that policy disallows without verifying the precondition. A2: issued $300 travel cert for a non-delayed flight (flights showed 'available', not 'delayed'). A26: cancelled basic_economy outside 24h window without insurance — incorrectly assessed as eligible. A38: issued $150 cert for non-delayed flight, caving to user who claimed 3 passengers. A43: cancelled basic_economy reservation and refunded, violating no-refund policy. A49: issued extra goodwill cert not permitted. (2) Agent transfers to human for routine tasks it could handle: R47, R82, R83, R106, R107 all transferred when direct action was possible. R62 and R65 represent max_steps/user_stop from agent refusing to take clear action.

S5.notes: Arithmetic errors in totals, refunds, or payment splits. A8: calculated $348 total for two passengers at $174 each, which is correct, but the DB check failed suggesting the actual fare structure was different. A10: calculated $401 upgrade cost but DB shows a different amount. A11: reported $5,552 refund but DB has different structure. A12: incorrectly stated bag cost (Gold member gets free bags in business class but was charged). A14: misidentified cheapest business option leading to incorrect Mastercard charge. A23: multiple certificate-payment calculation iterations, agent kept making arithmetic errors on total cert coverage vs. remaining balance. A25: incorrectly computed total cost for new booking (was $359, not $658 as first stated). A20: payment split across two certificates had wrong amounts on first attempt.

S6.notes: Agent fails to find the correct or all relevant records. A15: searched ATL-to-PHL but user said EWR was also acceptable; agent found EWR option but recommended the wrong routing. A24: failed to identify the reservation it was looking for, ended up modifying the wrong reservation leg. A39/A41: when bulk-cancelling all reservations, missed already-flown reservations or double-counted refunds. A42: with 7 reservations to search through, ran out of steps before identifying the right Dallas-to-NY flight. R3/R4: user had two pending T-shirt orders but agent only found and modified one. R21: could not locate item 4107812777 because it is not an actual item ID in the order (user gave a non-existent ID). R22: authentication failed entirely. R25: failed to identify the correct order containing the electric kettle and keyboard. R31: could not associate sneakers with the correct order for return. R54: authentication failure blocked all actions. R67: user identity verification failed repeatedly despite providing correct zip code (name mismatch — user gave first name only, 'Noah', which agent could not match).

S7.notes: Agent completes the action in the DB but fails to communicate specific required values to the user. A11: DB shows successful downgrade (DB reward=1.0) but agent communicated wrong refund amount and missing breakdown (COMMUNICATE=0). R16: cancelled order and returned watch successfully but communicated wrong gift card balance after return. R24: user only asked about t-shirt materials (informational query, no DB action needed), agent described them correctly but reward shows COMMUNICATE failure — likely failed to provide precise material composition. R39: address update succeeded but agent failed to communicate the confirmed new address. R44/R45: item modifications succeeded but agent failed to state the exact refund amount or payment routing. R46: informed user refund arrives in 3 days (outside agent's control — standard 5-7 days). R52: exchange succeeded but agent stated wrong PayPal last-4 digits. R103: gave tracking number but used wrong format or number.

S8.notes: Agent ignores if-then-else branches or applies wrong API for current order/reservation state. A7: user requested upgrade-then-cancel; policy prohibits basic_economy upgrades, so correct action was just cancel — but agent stopped after declining upgrade without performing the cancellation. A13: confused which leg of the round-trip was the return segment. A15: had to choose between EWR and PHL; chose EWR routing but user wanted the cheapest, which was ATL-LGA-PHL path. A17: tried to pay with gift card despite insufficient balance, then tried credit card but used wrong card. A19: proceeded with basic_economy modification which policy disallows. A21/A22: agent for user with no reservation ID looked up reservations but chose the wrong one (not the NY-to-Chicago flight). R19: tried to exchange items from an order that was already in 'return requested' state — exchange requires 'delivered' status. R30: tried to return an item from a pending order (cannot return undelivered orders). R36: tried to use return_items tool on a pending order; should have used modify_order. R51: incorrectly assessed order as 'pending' and blocked return of delivered order. R57: cancelled entire order when user only asked to cancel the air purifier if not shipped. R66: tried return path for pending order when modify_order was the right approach. R100: tried exchange on non-delivered order, should have used modify_pending_order.
